# cato Provider

The Cato Open Source Software provider is used to interact with resources supported by Cato Networks. The provider needs to be configured with the proper API credentials before it can be used.

The current API that the Cato provider is calling requires sequential execution. You can either use `depends_on` or specify the `parallelism` flag. Cato recommends the latter and setting the value to `1`. Example call: `terraform apply -parallelism=1`.

At startup, the provider performs a best-effort check for a newer stable version and emits a non-blocking warning when one is available. The check has a two-second default timeout and can be configured with `version_check_timeout_seconds` or `CATO_VERSION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (for example, `CATO_VERSION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5 terraform plan`). To opt out, set `version_check_disabled = true` in provider configuration or set any non-empty `CATO_VERSION_CHECK_DISABLED` environment variable value.

Use the navigation to the left to read about the available resources.

## Authentication

Choose one authentication method:

1. **Explicit credentials:** set `token` and `account_id` in the provider block, or use `CATO_TOKEN` and `CATO_ACCOUNT_ID`. Configure `baseurl` in the provider block or through `CATO_BASEURL`. Provider attributes override their environment values.
2. **catocli profile:** set `profile` in the provider block or `CATO_PROFILE` in the environment. The provider reads `cato_token`, `account_id`, and `endpoint` from that profile in `~/.cato/credentials`. Override the file path with `CATO_CREDENTIALS_FILE`. A selected profile overrides ambient credential environment variables; an explicit `baseurl` attribute overrides its endpoint.

A selected profile cannot be combined with `token` or `account_id` attributes in the provider block. This produces a diagnostic instead of silently switching accounts. For CI, use explicit credentials through environment variables and leave `CATO_PROFILE` unset.

```terraform
# Explicit configuration (unchanged)
provider "cato" {
  baseurl    = "https://api.catonetworks.com/api/v1/graphql2"
  token      = "xxxxxxx"
  account_id = "xxxxxxx"
}

# catocli profile based authentication
provider "cato" {
  profile = "refarch-dev"
}
```

```sh
# or resolve the profile from the environment instead of the provider block
export CATO_PROFILE=refarch-dev
terraform plan
```

Using a catocli profile means Terraform reads the same `~/.cato/credentials` file catocli itself uses (the file `catocli configure set` writes) -- no tokens need to live in `*.tfvars` or shell exports, and switching tenants is just a matter of switching `profile` (or `CATO_PROFILE`) to a different profile name. For CI or tests that shouldn't depend on the invoking user's real credentials file, point `CATO_CREDENTIALS_FILE` at an alternate path.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Configuration based authentication
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cato = {
      source  = "catonetworks/cato"
    }
  }
}

provider "cato" {
  baseurl                = "https://api.catonetworks.com/api/v1/graphql2"
  token                  = "xxxxxxx"
  account_id             = "xxxxxxx"
  retry_max              = 5
  retry_wait_min_seconds = 1
  retry_wait_max_seconds = 30
  # Optional: disable the advisory Registry version check.
  # version_check_disabled = true
  # Optional: maximum time for the advisory Registry version check.
  # version_check_timeout_seconds = 2
}

# Alternative: catocli profile based authentication. Instead of baseurl/token/account_id
# above, point at a profile name from the catocli credentials file (~/.cato/credentials
# by default; override with CATO_CREDENTIALS_FILE). See the "Authentication" section of
# the provider README for the full resolution order.
# provider "cato" {
#   profile = "refarch-dev"
# }

resource "cato_socket_site" "site1" {
  name            = "SOCKET Site - X1700"
  description     = "SOCKET Site - X1700"
  site_type       = "DATACENTER"
  connection_type = "SOCKET_X1700"

  native_range = {
    native_network_range = "192.168.37.0/24"
    local_ip             = "192.168.37.5"
    interface_dest_type = "LAN"
    dhcp_settings = {
      dhcp_type = "DHCP_RANGE"
      ip_range  = "192.168.37.100-192.168.37.150"
    }
  }

  site_location = {
    country_code = "FR"
    timezone     = "Europe/Paris"
  }
}

resource "cato_static_host" "host" {
  site_id = cato_socket_site.site1.id
  name    = "test-terraform"
  ip      = "192.168.25.24"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AccountId for the Cato API (can be provided via the CATO_ACCOUNT_ID environment variable). Part of the explicit-credentials method; mutually exclusive with `profile`.
- `baseurl` (String) URL for the Cato API. Can be provided using CATO_BASEURL environment variable.
- `profile` (String) Name of a catocli profile to source credentials from. When set (or when CATO_PROFILE is set), the provider reads token, account_id, and endpoint from the named section of the catocli credentials file (~/.cato/credentials by default; override the path with the CATO_CREDENTIALS_FILE environment variable). This is the local-development auth method and is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with token/account_id attributes in the provider block. A selected profile overrides ambient CATO_TOKEN, CATO_ACCOUNT_ID, and CATO_BASEURL values; an explicit baseurl attribute still wins. For CI use the explicit-credentials env vars instead. See the provider README's Authentication section.
- `retry_max` (Number) Maximum number of retries for retryable API requests. Defaults to 5. Can be provided using CATO_RETRY_MAX environment variable.
- `retry_wait_max_seconds` (Number) Maximum backoff between retry attempts, in seconds. Defaults to 30. Can be provided using CATO_RETRY_WAIT_MAX_SECONDS environment variable.
- `retry_wait_min_seconds` (Number) Minimum backoff between retry attempts, in seconds. Defaults to 1. Can be provided using CATO_RETRY_WAIT_MIN_SECONDS environment variable.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) API Key for the Cato API (can be provided via the CATO_TOKEN environment variable). Part of the explicit-credentials method; mutually exclusive with `profile`.
- `version_check_disabled` (Boolean) Disables the advisory Terraform Registry version check. Can be provided using CATO_VERSION_CHECK_DISABLED environment variable; any non-empty value disables the check.
- `version_check_timeout_seconds` (Number) Maximum time for the advisory Terraform Registry version check, in seconds. Defaults to 2. Can be provided using CATO_VERSION_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable.
